facts: Principle 19 of the book is 'Use Feedback to Your Advantage'.
Canfield compares the path to a goal with a flight: the plane is off its exact course most of the time and the pilot keeps correcting from the instruments' feedback until it arrives.
Feedback tells you when you are drifting off track and need to correct course.
People around you often hold feedback back because they fear you will react badly, so you have to ask for it.
Canfield recommends a direct question: 'On a scale of 1 to 10, how would you rate the quality of our relationship (service/product)?'
He says he asks his wife and his coworkers a version of this question every week.
A second question he suggests: 'In what ways do you see me holding myself back?' He advises taking the answer gracefully.
An answer below 10 usually comes with specific suggestions for what would make it better.
scene_details: a pilot correcting from the instruments while the plane drifts
a weekly question to his wife: a number from 1 to 10
tension: Feedback is the thing that keeps you on course, yet the people who could give it usually stay quiet unless asked.
opening_idea: Start with the number: once a week Canfield asks his own wife to rate their relationship from 1 to 10.

lessons.idea: Ask for a number, then ask what would raise it; a specific question gets an answer people otherwise keep to themselves.
lessons.anchor: The weekly 1-to-10 question to his wife and coworkers.

lessons.idea: Being off course is normal; staying off course comes from not asking.

reflect_final: Who could tell you something useful about your work or relationship this week, and what number question would you ask them?

use_cases.situation: End of a project with a client
use_cases.move: Ask the client to rate the work from 1 to 10 and what would have made it higher.

use_cases.situation: A quiet evening with your partner
use_cases.move: Borrow Canfield's weekly habit: ask for a number for the past week, then listen without defending.
Ask for a 1-to-10 rating on one specific deliverable and one change that would add a point.

pocket_idea: Canfield asks his wife for a weekly number from 1 to 10; ask yours, and listen to what's missing.

conversation_variants.question_idea: Who have you never asked for honest feedback?
